cards.title: AUC Estimation via Linear Combinations of Mean Concentrations
cards.claim: In destructive sampling designs, the AUC for a specific dosing regimen can be estimated using linear combinations of mean concentrations measured at discrete time points, rather than integrating individual subject trajectories.
conditions: Experimental unit must be sacrificed to obtain concentration data (destructive/terminal sampling).
Multiple subjects are sampled at each time point to allow calculation of mean concentrations.
The method applies to metabolite or drug concentration over time.
required_inputs: Mean concentration values at specific time points for each dosing regimen.
Time points at which samples were collected.
Sample sizes per time point (implied for variance estimation, though not explicitly detailed in abstract).
limitations: Abstract does not specify the exact weighting scheme or variance estimation method for the linear combination.
Applicability to non-uniform time spacing or complex designs requires checking the full method details (not available in abstract).
cards.downstream_use: Interpreting group-level PK parameters from terminal sacrifice studies. Validating whether reported AUCs in such studies are derived from this or similar group-mean based methods.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
